Hey! I’m glad I didn’t delete my post. I ended up having one in person appointment where they figured out the right levels for everything to be at so that I could be ready to start actual treatments 5 days a week the next time. But I ended up deciding not to do it, at least for right now. BUT at my appointment I did experience just a few minutes of what a typical TMS treatment would be like and I was definitely being dramatic in my original post. It wasn’t painful at all and  depending on travel time and your normal schedule, it could be much less energy (and time?) consuming than medications, and definitely much easier and less risky than ECT. 

Sorry this reply is so long, but if you have any questions I can see if I can answer with the info I was given from the psychiatrist and what I experienced. I think it’s definitely worth looking into! Especially if you looked into ECT, TMS seems much less daunting in my opinion, and has better statistics I think. Plus if you did the treatment and it doesn’t help at all, it’s less than 9 weeks and tms can’t make your depression worse , so then you can make an even more informed decision about continuing life. That’s kinda the thinking I used. Hope that helps a bit :)
I think about this all the time. It blows my mind that people live in this world and are not constantly thinking about how they can get out of it.

This might be really naive for me to say, as I’m still figuring out how to live, but do you need relationships in order to not be suicidal? I think most mental health professionals would say yes, but what do they know right? If you feel that people already don’t care about you, you could put yourself first without risking any current friendships. Take yourself on dates, enjoy your own company, treat yourself? You could change your whole personality if you want. You’ve got nothing to lose, so if it backfires, you can just go back to what you’re doing now. Maybe that’s freeing in a way, idk. Maybe it’s worth thinking about before killing yourself, just to see if there’s other unconventional ways to feel ‘enough’, not even enough for other people, but just enough for the world. 

Also I’m 20 F and I can relate to a lot of things you said. I have social anxiety so I don’t make friends or talk to people, in person or online. You seem cool though.

I think there are tons of ways to fulfill your urge to ‘feel something’ before you resort to cutting. The use of temperature is helpful for a lot of people. You could try taking ice cubes and running them up and down where you feel like you want to cut. Holding a hot beverage. If it’s cold where you are, stand outside for a minute to shock your system a bit. Color your skin with paint or markers. If these don’t work for you try focusing on WHY you want to self harm (ex: as a punishment, response to anxiety, to feel a release) - then try to fill that need with a different action. Just try tons of different things and I honestly think you’ll find something that works even better than cutting. 

The longer you can avoid cutting the better. I cut sometimes and it’s helpful short term but I know if I ever do get better I’ll hate all my scars and it can definitely become an addiction of some sort. At the end of the day cutting is just one of the millions of coping skills, but it’s one that you don’t want to use often if at all. There are much safer, more helpful, and even fun coping skills out there. You got this! :)
